newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-OLAJUWON BOOSTS ROCKETS OVER BULLS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-OLAJUWON BOOSTS ROCKETS OVER BULLS.

text.p: Hakeem Olajuwon and the Houston Rockets played like champions Sunday, holding the Chicago Bulls scoreless for more than seven minutes in claiming a 102-86 victory for their seventh win in eight games.
Olajuwon had 32 points and 16 rebounds and the Houston Rockets held the Chicago Bulls scoreless for over seven minutes in a 102-86 victory, their seventh in eight games.

"I'm very happy with the way it came out," Olajuwon said. "When you play against the champions, you've got to come out and play well. The team was focused in the locker room before the game. It was a war out there."

Playing without injured forward Charles Barkley, the Rockets held the Bulls to a meaningless basket over the final 7:12 and avenged a 24-point loss in Chicago eight days ago. The loss ended the Bulls' nine-game winning streak.
The conference leaders split the season series and will not meet again unless they advance to the NBA Finals. Houston (31-9) and Chicago (34-5) have won the last six championships.

Kevin Willis filled in for Barkley with a season-high 20 points and eight rebounds. He took advantage of the absence of Bulls forward Dennis Rodman, the league's rebound leader, who was suspended for at least 11 games for kicking a cameraman.

Olajuwon shot 14-of-25 from the field and added five blocks and four steals. He played the entire game without drinking any water, which is forbidden during daylight hours of the extended Moslem holiday of Ramadan.
"What Mr. Olajuwon did today, to play that well without drinking a drop of water during the game, was the most amazing thing I've ever seen in my life," Barkley said afterwards.

Michael Jordan had 26 points and a season-high 14 rebounds for the Bulls, who had won their last four meetings with the Rockets. Forwards Scottie Pippen and Toni Kukoc combined for just eight points on woeful 3-of-24 shooting.
In Miami, Penny Hardaway scored 19 points and dished out six assists to lead the Orlando Magic to a 99-87 victory over interstate rivals the Miami Heat.
Dennis Scott and Nick Anderson each added 18 points for the Magic, who finished their road trip 4-1. Orlando (16-19) made up for a 20-point loss to Miami (28-11) last month.
"We've shown glimpses, and if we have everyone healthy, we can beat anyone in the league," said Hardaway. "Beating the Heat is a great victory for us."
Voshon Lenard had 21 points, while Alonzo Mourning and P.J. Brown had 14 points and 11 rebounds apiece for Miami.

In Vancouver, rookie Shareef Abdur-Rahim scored 26 points and Blue Edwards added 11 of his 13 in the fourth quarter as the Vancouver Grizzlies snapped a five-game losing streak by defeating their expansion rival Toronto Raptors 100-92.
Anthony Peeler added 17 points and George Lynch had 12 and 13 rebounds for the league-worst Grizzlies (8-32).

At Indiana, Reggie Miller and Rik Smits scored 20 points apiece as the Indiana Pacers built a 25-point third-quarter lead and hung on for a 111-107 victory over the Philadelphia 76ers, who dropped their 12th straight game.
Derrick McKey added 17 points for Indiana.
Rookie Allen Iverson scored a career-high 37 points, including 18 in the final period for the spiralling 76ers, who have lost 22 of their lst 23 games.
In Los Angeles, Chris Mills hit consecutive three-pointers in the second overtime as the Cleveland Cavaliers snapped a six-game losing skid by trimming the Clippers 107-102.
Bobby Phills scored 25 points and Mark West added 16 points and 14 rebounds for the Cavs.
Vaught finished with 21 points and 11 rebounds for the Clippers, who have dropped four straight after a season-high four-game winning streak.
In Portland, Kenny Anderson scored 12 of his 26 points in the fourth quarter, when the Portland Trail Blazers rallied past the Utah Jazz 102-96 for their eighth win in 10 games.

Arvydas Sabonis scored 22 points and Isaiah Rider added 21 for the Blazers, who trailed 76-69 entering the final period. Portland has wins over quality teams such as Houston, Detroit, the Los Angeles Lakers and Utah during its hot streak.
Jeff Hornacek scored 22 points and Karl Malone added 17 for the Jazz, who had a three-game winning streak halted.
